answer: A mesa registry issues identity slots only after hardware attestation and a bond; rewards are linear in bonded capital, but each slot pays a fixed fee and must answer a random comet beacon challenge. Splitting capital across N slots earns the same linear bond yield while paying N fees and N attestation costs, so splitting does not increase rewards. Fake slots must sustain attestations and challenge responses; a whisper gossip layer flags duplicate attestations. Limitations: compromised hardware or colluding attestors can still mint slots, and fixed costs only deter low-value splits.
